_comment: Shared oracle for the derive-profile ceiling formula, asserted by BOTH services/api/internal/config/derive_profile_golden_test.go and bench/derive/tests/profile-test.py. The bench computes -max-prompt-bytes from a profile; memoire computes the same number from the same registry file. A drift between the two would bench a different window than production runs — the comparison's whole premise (docs/DERIVE-PROFILE-DESIGN.md). Cases are exact integers, not tolerances: floor() has no tolerance.

cases.name: bench-9b-rebench
cases.why: the geometry the 2026-08-25 re-bench is planned at

cases.name: autopsy-geometry
cases.why: the failed run's own numbers: 34918 is the ceiling that would have kept prompt + completion inside the 32768 context, against the 70000 actually sent

cases.name: rounding-boundary
cases.why: 50 * 2.3 is 114.99999999999999 in IEEE doubles, so the honest floor is 114 — the case that catches a reordered expression on either side

cases.name: large-context
cases.why: a 64k serving context at the denser 2.3 ratio

cases.name: minimal-room
cases.why: one token of prompt room is legal geometry, and must not round to zero
